text:
incidentbot: P1 — models-west1 serving 503 spike. Multiple customers reporting 503s. Incident ticket: INC-4821. Paging oncall: alexg, mariap. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-4821

Alex G: I'm on it. Seeing ~30% 503 rate across model-server pods in west1 (svc=model-serving). No obvious errors in LB yet. Starting quick triage.

Vikram S: thx. any correlation with deploys?

Alex G: no deploys in last 2h. CPU steady. Error appears in app logs: upstream connections failing with ECONNRESET from model-worker process. Rolling restart of problematic replica group now to see if it recovers.

Alex G: immediate checks i'm running:
```bash
kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-server -o wide
kubectl -n serving logs -l app=model-server --tail 200 | grep -i "error"
ps aux | grep model_worker
```

Maria P: I'll be taking over driver role at my shift change in ~10min (00:00 UTC). Vikram, can you own comms during the handoff window? I can take full driver after 00:00.

Vikram S: I can do comms. I'll draft an external note and keep #customers-updates updated.

Alex G: summary for handoff:
- Impact: 503s for ~30% of requests in west1; affected customers: tenant-alpha, beta-saas, internal QA cluster (partial).
- Mitigation so far: rolling restart of the 3 failing pods started at 1746501300, 1/3 restarted cleanly, 2 still showing restarts
- Suspected cause: transient upstream worker crashes (ECONNRESET).
- Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-serving#503-spike (see sections "Immediate mitigation" and "When to escalate to eng-runtime").

Alex G: Vikram — please post ETA and request to customers if this will affect SLAs. Maria — next steps after handoff: watch health endpoints and autoscaler, check kv-cache warmup for high-latency tails.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled shift change for Maria P at 00:00 UTC (10 minutes). Current on-call window: Alex G -> Maria P.

Alex G: OFFICIAL HANDOFF (1746501500): driver -> Maria P (starting 00:00 UTC). comms -> Vikram S. Known state: restarts partly applied, error rate down from 40% to ~28% after first pod restart. No customer-facing workarounds yet. If restarts don't converge in 15m escalate to eng-runtime and consider rolling scale-up. :white_check_mark:

Maria P: taking driver. immediate checklist I'm running now:
- curl health endpoints across 5 pods
- tail logs for repeating trace IDs
- check HPA scale events and node pressure
- confirm restart sequence completed

Vikram S: DRAFT to customers (LMK edits):
"We're investigating a partial outage in west1 impacting model-serving (some requests returning 503). We're performing rolling restarts and monitoring. Estimated recovery time: 15-30 minutes. We'll update here and via support tickets. —Vikram, oncall comms"

Alex G: include note that tenant-alpha is seeing the highest error rate and a temporary retry increase on client side reduces visible errors (internal workaround). Also mention we're not rolling back any deploys.

Maria P: got it. I'm seeing HPA spike at 00:03 UTC, node cpu ~78% on 2 nodes. Restarts completed at 00:05 UTC for all pods, error rate dropped to ~6%. Continuing to monitor for 10 more minutes.

Vikram S: sent external blurb to affected customers and support queue. I'll ping again when we're green.

Alex G: thanks team. Maria, if it re-regresses escalate to eng-runtime and open INC-4821 update with logs and pod-ids.

Maria P: acknowledged. I'll keep driver for the next 30m and then hand back if stable. Updating incident ticket now with timeline and commands run.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-4821 updated: status = mitigated (partial). Next check in 10m.
